Here is the foundational summary to help anchor everyone's work on Quick Swap. 

The core problem is that replacing a planned meal currently takes too much effort; our goal is to let users effortlessly swap a scheduled recipe with an alternative from their saved preferences. For the primary flow, I propose the user taps a "Swap" icon on a planned meal, which opens a bottom sheet displaying a few recommended alternatives. Tapping "Select" on one of these options will instantly replace the original meal in the weekly view and trigger our success tracking event. The most critical edge cases we need to design and build for are handling users with zero saved preferences (potentially falling back to popular recipes) and managing prompt updates to the user's grocery list if it was already generated. Hopefully, this provides a clear starting point so Design can finalize interactions, Data and Engineering can align on event tracking, and Support can begin drafting their macros.

**Quick Swap User Stories: The Definition of Done**

Okay, so the task is to craft 3-5 user stories, complete with acceptance criteria, for the new Quick Swap feature within the MealPlanr app, all within a tight five-sentence limit. I need these to act as a shared definition of "done" for the entire team – Design, Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Support. First, the core flow: "As a user, I want to quickly replace a planned meal with a saved preference; this is complete when tapping 'Swap' opens a bottom sheet of personalized alternatives, selecting one instantly updates the weekly view, and the required success/abandonment tracking events fire."

Then, we need to address the "no preferences" edge case: "As a user without saved preferences, I want to see fallback options so I can still change my plan; this is done when the sheet displays trending popular recipes alongside a brief UI prompt encouraging the user to save preferences for better future recommendations."

Finally, grocery list synchronization is key: "As a user with an already-generated grocery list, I want my list to update automatically upon swapping so I buy the right ingredients; this is satisfied when the system seamlessly adds the new recipe's ingredients and removes items unique to the discarded meal." With these, we have a clear definition for everyone.

These criteria will guide our design review tomorrow, help finalize the event schema, and give engineering clear boundaries for their upcoming sprint implementation.
rounds.response: To serve as our shared definition of done across design, engineering, data, and support, here are the three core user stories and their acceptance criteria for Quick Swap. **Core Swap:** As a user, I want to quickly replace a planned meal with a saved preference; this is complete when tapping "Swap" opens a bottom sheet of personalized alternatives, selecting one instantly updates the weekly view, and the required data tracking events accurately fire. **No Preferences:** As a user without saved preferences, I want to see fallback options so I can still easily change my plan; this is done when the bottom sheet displays trending recipes alongside a brief UI prompt encouraging the user to save preferences for better future matches. **Grocery List Sync:** As a user with an already-generated grocery list, I want my list to update automatically upon swapping so I buy the right ingredients; this is satisfied when the system seamlessly adds the new recipe's ingredients and immediately removes items unique to the discarded meal. These criteria will guide our design review tomorrow, help finalize the data schema, and give engineering clear, testable boundaries for their upcoming sprint implementation.
